brief: This filament rack is already built: four spool bays, each with a spool axle across it, and open bins on the pillar tops. Do not change the parts. Dress it for use: a 1 kg filament spool hanging on every axle, and a few small printing tools in the open top bins.

requirements.requirement: Do not change parts (existing build unchanged)
requirements.evidence: No place/remove ops performed; get_build parts unchanged (19 pieces, 4 axles, 9 bins etc). Only props added via hang_spools and dress.

requirements.requirement: 1 kg filament spool hanging on every spool axle (four bays)
requirements.evidence: hang_spools placed 4x filament-spool on axle:2#0,0#5, axle:2#0,2#5, axle:2#0,4#5, axle:2#0,6#5 - all 4 axles now occupied.

requirements.requirement: Few small printing tools in the open top bins on pillar tops
requirements.evidence: Dressed bins at level 2: bin:0,0,2 heap-nuts-div3, bin:0,2,2 heap-screws-div3, bin:0,4,2 heap-standoffs-div3 - small workshop/printing consumables that fit the narrow div3 compartments (46mm compartments). Larger tools refused PROP_NO_REST due to cell wall overlap.

finish.summary: Filament rack dressed without altering parts: 4 filament spools hung on all axles via hang_spools, and three top bins filled with small printing consumables (M3 nuts/screws/standoffs div3) that fit the div3 compartments. Larger tools overhang cell walls and cannot rest.

Edge cap · female, two stories tall

M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
